review.rationale: The mature Dhoni–Raina core, supported by Bravo and Jadeja, combines strong participation, competitiveness and balanced pace-spin construction as the clearest Expansion-era CSK representation.
The 2011 side preserves the later Deccan identity through Dhawan, Sangakkara, Duminy, Steyn, Mishra and Ojha in a legal, balanced representative XI.
The table-leading 2012 Delhi side captures the Sehwag-led identity with Jayawardene, Pietersen and Morkel while retaining credible keeper and bowling coverage.
Kochi’s only season is represented by its recognizable McCullum–Jayawardene–Jadeja core, with legal keeper and overseas construction and a credible pace-spin attack.
The 2012 XI is the first fully recognizable Gambhir–Narine-era KKR and preserves the historically defining title-season core despite not maximizing Team Evaluation.
The 2013 XI captures Mumbai’s first-title transition through Tendulkar, Rohit, Pollard, Malinga and Johnson with strong continuity and complete bowling coverage.
The 2011 XI is Pune Warriors’ most recognizable and functional representation, centered on Yuvraj, Uthappa and Ryder with a more credible overall construction than 2012.
The 2011 XI captures the Gilchrist–Marsh Punjab batting identity while retaining Karthik as keeper and a varied attack led by Harris, Chawla and Praveen Kumar.
The 2013 XI represents Rajasthan’s Dravid–Rahane–Watson core and playoff run, with Samson emerging and a credible mixed bowling attack.
The 2011 XI preserves the formative Gayle–Kohli–de Villiers identity and Final run, making it more historically representative than the higher-rated 2013 alternative.
The inaugural 2013 Sunrisers side preserves the franchise’s early Dhawan-led batting and Steyn–Mishra bowling identity in a legal representative XI.
